aim: This autumn our main aim was to improve your writing: to write the right message for the right reader, from a quick text to a friend to a polite email and an Instagram caption for your salon.

lessons.title: Text Me Back
lessons.studied: Reading a real chat for the main idea and details; 30+ text abbreviations (BTW, TBH, ASAP, ETA, L8R); what makes a good reply; who you can send text-speak to; decoding and writing short messages.
lessons.language: WYD rn? · HBU? · IDK · TTYL · CU Sat · np

lessons.title: Sincerely Yours
lessons.studied: Formal, semi-formal and informal register; the same news as a text and as an email; rules for formal writing (no abbreviations, full forms, clear subject line); polite requests; fixing a badly written email; email ping-pong.
lessons.language: I am writing to… · Could you please…? · I look forward to hearing from you. · Kind regards

lessons.title: Caption This
lessons.topic: Instagram captions for your hair studio
lessons.studied: Stopping the scroll; the anatomy of a caption (hook, story, call to action, hashtags); hooks; writing tips; words that sell; fixing a caption; writing your own salon posts in English.
lessons.language: Okay, real talk… · Save this for your next salon visit. · Tell me in the comments…

lessons.title: A Year in Writing
lessons.studied: Writing about your birthday, your year and your goals as a text, an email and a caption; present perfect for "this year" vs past simple for finished time; spend time + -ing; manage / hope / plan + to; making sentences sound B2.
lessons.language: So far, I have… · I haven't… yet · I finally managed to… · I hope to… · Although… / However…

lessons.title: And the Award Goes To
lessons.topic: Speaking: giving an interview and an award speech
lessons.studied: Reading a winner's magazine interview; an interview toolkit (buy time, be honest, give an example, say thank you, show feelings); A + R + E answers; award vocabulary with word stress; stress patterns; pauses, stress and falling intonation in a short speech; answering interview questions in one minute.
lessons.language: That's a good question. · I'd say… · It hasn't sunk in yet. · I'm over the moon. · I'm deeply honoured. · I couldn't have done it without…

reviews.label: 15 October

corrections.why: tired of + noun / -ing: "I'm tired of waiting."
Fixed phrase: "Sorry, I'm in a rush."
Use the adjective for how you feel.

words: collect or build up over time
a machine that heats water at home
I feel relaxed after a massage.
something you are not good at
I left home in a rush.
She was distressed after the news.
a small metal object fired from a gun
companies from Europe that sell goods
We buy products from European vendors.
putting words on paper or screen
Writing in English is hard for me.
a voice in a video from someone you don't see

reviews.label: 26 October

corrections.why: "The dog wagged its tail." / "It's cold today."

words: interested in other people's private business
I'm a bit nosy, I always ask questions.
throw away or remove something you don't want
I want to get rid of old clothes.
go to an event or class
I attend English lessons twice a week.
don't see or think of me as…
They don't perceive me as a beginner.
a person in charge of workers
I need to ask my supervisor.

reviews.label: 2 November

corrections.why: "A person" = he/she, so the verb takes -s: doesn't.
Fixed phrase: at the same time = одночасно.

words: the title at the top of a text
Bright colours can draw my attention.
The results were better than expected.
I can't cook and talk at the same time.

reviews.label: 26 November

corrections.why: Use the adjective: it was successful. "I was a success" means you as a person were a success.
Short adjectives take -er without more: faster, bigger, easier.

words: a difficult choice between two options
I faced a real dilemma: stay or move?
at a moment when you must make a big decision
I'm at the crossroads in my career.
a natural feeling that makes you act to save your life
A life-saving instinct made her jump back.
respect someone and want to be like them
I really admire my first boss.
feeling very sorry for something wrong you did
He felt deep remorse for what he did.
a hard hat that protects your head
Always wear a helmet on a bike.
a famous person you admire very much
a soft way to give your opinion
I would say attention to detail is my strength.
It took a mere five minutes.
maternity leave, maternity hospital / being a mother

going_well: You finished all four Writing Studio lessons: texts, formal emails, Instagram captions and the revision lesson.
You can now choose the right style for the reader: text-speak for friends, full polite sentences for a manager or a client.
You bring real life into English (your salon, work, suppliers, the news), so your vocabulary is growing fast: 23 new words and phrases in three lessons.
You write captions for your own hair posts, which is the most useful writing practice you can do.

focus.do: After he, she, it and a person, check the verb: doesn't, has, likes, works.
Learn them as one block: tired of, in a rush, at the same time. Practise them in the "From our lessons" flashcards.
Use I'm + adjective: I'm stressed, I'm relaxed, I'm exhausted, I'm distressed.
Before you send a text or a caption, read it once more: can you say "it is"? Then write it's.

focus.why: the key B2 grammar for writing about your year
focus.do: hope to / manage to / plan to + verb; spend time + -ing; past simple with finished time (last month, in June).
Tap Listen on each new word in the flashcards and repeat the stressed syllable louder.

next_steps: Do Flashcards, Learn and a Test for each word set at least once a week; your teacher gets every test result.
Write one Instagram caption in English for your salon each week and bring it to the lesson.
Write one short formal email a week (to a supplier, a landlord or a client) and check it against the formal writing rules from Lesson 2.

homework.lesson: Lesson 5 · And the Award Goes To
homework.note: Do these before Monday's lesson and send your recording to your teacher. Tick each task when it is done. Your drafts stay on this device.
homework.phrasesTitle: Speech steps and phrases from the lesson
phrases: 1 · Thank the organisers: I'd like to thank …
2 · Say how you feel: I'm deeply honoured. / I'm over the moon. / It hasn't sunk in yet.
3 · Thank your team and clients: I couldn't have done it without … / A big thank you to …
4 · One sentence about the future: I can't wait for … / I'm hoping to …
Words: award-winning · grateful · recognition · achievement · signature style · attention to detail · behind the scenes

tasks.title: Write your real thank-you speech
tasks.detail: Write your real one-minute thank-you speech for Best Wedding Hairstylist of the Year. Use the four steps from stage 8 of the lesson.
tasks.check: Four steps · three words from the flashcards · short sentences · end with a thank-you

tasks.title: Mark it and practise it
tasks.detail: In your speech, mark the pauses (/ short, // long) and write the stressed words in CAPITALS. Then read it out loud three times: slowly, with pauses, and with your voice going down at the end of each sentence.

tasks.title: Record it and send it
tasks.detail: Record your speech as a voice message and send it to your teacher. Smile while you speak: people can hear it!

tasks.title: Find an award winner's interview
tasks.detail: Find a short interview with an award winner online. Write down three phrases you like and the link.

phrases: I spent most of my time + verb-ing
So far, I have + past participle
It didn't go to plan, but …
My goal for next year is + to + verb
By my next birthday, I'd like + to + verb

tasks.title: Finish the Writing studio task you didn't do in class
tasks.detail: Choose the task you didn't finish in class (A, B or C) and use two phrases from stage 4 (below).

options.name: Task A · Text message
options.brief: Your friend Kate writes: “hbd!!! what r u doing to celebrate? how's life? miss u”. Reply to Kate. Say how you celebrated, tell her one thing about your year and suggest meeting up. Abbreviations are fine.
options.check: Friendly tone · short sentences · answer all her questions · a question back

options.name: Task B · Formal email
options.brief: Think of one goal for next year. Write to a school or academy about a course that can help you reach it. Say why you are writing, explain your goal briefly and ask about dates, price and a certificate.
options.check: Dear … · I am writing to … · polite questions · no abbreviations · Yours faithfully / sincerely

options.name: Task C · Instagram caption
options.brief: Write a birthday post for your page, like Sofia's. Start with a hook. Tell a short story of your year: what you did, what you achieved, what is not done yet. Finish with your next goal and a question for your followers.
options.check: Hook in line one · past and future · two phrases from stage 4 · call to action

tasks.title: A letter to yourself
tasks.detail: Write a letter to yourself to open on your next birthday. What did you do this year? What do you hope to achieve by then?

tasks.title: Feeling brave? (optional)
tasks.detail: Post your birthday caption in English. Next lesson, tell me how people reacted.
